title: Tanzanian Sesame Balls
community: Coastal Tanzania — the sesame sweet tradition
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Tanzanian Sesame Balls — toasted sesame seeds bound together with caramelised sugar and honey, rolled into small firm balls with a cardamom note. The sesame sweet of the Tanzanian coast — crunchy, nutty, and deeply satisfying.
longDesc: Sesame balls are the simplest and most ancient Tanzanian coastal sweet — toasted sesame and caramelised sugar, a touch of cardamom, and the patience to roll them while warm. They are the sweet that has been made the same way on the Swahili coast for centuries.
ingredients: 1.5 cups sesame seeds — toasted until golden
steps: Toast sesame seeds in a dry pan until golden and fragrant. Cool slightly.
Combine sugar, honey, and water in a saucepan.
Cook over medium heat until the mixture reaches soft-ball stage (115°C).
Add toasted sesame seeds, cardamom, and salt. Stir to combine.
Working quickly with greased hands, roll into small balls (2cm).
chefTips: Work very quickly — the mixture sets fast.
Cool completely before storing — they stick to each other if warm.
cookingScience: See TZA199 for brittle candy sugar science. Honey in the mixture adds invertase and natural inverted sugar — this prevents the characteristic graininess of pure crystallised sugar candy, producing a smoother, less grainy sesame ball.
sustainabilityTips: Tanzania produces excellent sesame — locally grown.
storage: Airtight container 2 weeks separated by parchment.
healthBenefits: Sesame seeds are exceptionally rich in calcium.
culturalNote: Sesame balls are the sweet that has no ceremony around it — they are simply made and simply eaten, one of the oldest confections of the Swahili coast, unchanged across centuries.
